comp_0.description:
What it does The decision rule for the Sequential Executor: after each step it decides whether to carry on, loop again, or stop.

How it works On every pass it reads the current data, the iteration count and the exit conditions configured on the FSM, and returns the next state. It stops when an exit condition matches or the iteration ceiling is reached; otherwise it advances to the next slot. It makes no calls of its own and holds no configuration - it reads what the FSM was given.

Configure Nothing. Set the loop behaviour on the FSM instead.

In and out In: the run data, iteration count and exit conditions. Out: the next state, plus the reason when it decides to stop.

Use it when It comes with the Sequential Executor template. You do not add or configure it separately.
comp_0.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: policy
name: Sequential Executor Policy
description: >
  Internal control policy for the Sequential Executor. Evaluates the configured
  exit conditions after each loop iteration and decides whether to continue.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    request_data:
      data: object (optional) - The accumulated state data to test conditions against.
      exit_conditions: array (optional) - Field/operator/value tests to evaluate.
      iteration: integer (optional) - The iteration that just completed.
      max_iterations: integer (optional) - Hard iteration cap.
    response_data:
      should_exit: boolean - True when the loop should stop.
      exit_reason: string - Why the loop stopped, or null when it continues.

policy_states:
  - continue
  - exit
comp_0.name: SEQUENTIAL EXECUTOR - POLICY (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
comp_0.short_description: The decision rule for the Sequential Executor: after each step it decides whether to carry

comp_1.description:
What it does The exit of the Sequential Executor template. It returns what the sequence produced.

How it works Takes the data reaching it after the final step and returns it as the result of the nested run, so the parent flow can carry on with it. It adds nothing of its own.

Configure Nothing.

In and out In: the result of the last step. Out: the same data, as the template's result.

Use it when It comes with the Sequential Executor template. You do not add it separately.

comp_2.description:
What it does The entry point of the Sequential Executor template. It accepts the caller's input and hands it to the first step.

How it works Passes the incoming data and any accompanying file straight through to the executor, adding nothing. It exists because every orchestration needs exactly one start; it is not something you configure.

Configure Nothing.

In and out In: the caller's request. Out: the same, unchanged, into the first state slot.

Use it when It comes with the Sequential Executor template. You do not add it separately.

comp_3.description:
What it does The engine of the Sequential Executor template. It holds the ordered steps and drives them one after another.

How it works Each state slot holds one component. The FSM runs them in order, passing each result forward, and asks its policy after every step whether to continue, loop or finish. Looping repeats the whole sequence until an exit condition matches or the iteration ceiling is hit.

Configure
- States - the ordered slots and their components.
- Enable looping - repeat the sequence rather than running once.
- Max iterations - hard stop for a loop, so it cannot run away.
- Exit conditions - field, operator and value tests that end the loop when any one matches.
- Forward input to states - pass the original input to every step, not just the first.
- Flat accumulation - merge results into one object instead of nesting per step.

In and out In: the run's data. Out: the last step's result, or the accumulation of all steps.

Use it when It comes with the Sequential Executor template - configure it there rather than adding it on its own.
comp_3.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: fsm
name: Sequential Executor
description: >
  Executes its wired state slots one after another, in order. Enable looping to
  repeat the sequence until an exit condition is met or the iteration limit is
  reached. Output is namespaced by slot.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    artifact_type_input: optional(json)
    artifact_type_output: optional(json)
    response_data_contract: dynamic
    response_data_contract_reason: >-
      Slot keys are the port names named by the `states` input parameter (or the
      probed state_N ports when it is empty); only `input` is statically known.
    response_data:
      input: object - The executor's own inbound request_data, echoed back.
      state_1: object (optional) - response_data returned by the state_1 slot.
      state_2: object (optional) - response_data returned by the state_2 slot.
      state_3: object (optional) - response_data returned by the state_3 slot.
      state_4: object (optional) - response_data returned by the state_4 slot.

state_ports:
  - port_name: state_1
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
  - port_name: state_2
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
  - port_name: state_3
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
  - port_name: state_4
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none

policy_ports:
  - port_name: policy
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    response_data:
      should_exit: boolean - Whether the loop should stop after this iteration.
      exit_reason: string (optional) - Human-readable reason the loop stopped.

input_parameters:
  - name: enable_looping
    type: boolean
    label: Enable Looping
    default: false
    description: Repeat the whole sequence until the policy says to stop.
  - name: max_iterations
    type: integer
    label: Max Iterations
    default: 10
    description: Hard cap on loop iterations.
  - name: exit_conditions
    type: text_long
    label: Exit Conditions
    default: "[]"
    description: JSON array of field/operator/value tests evaluated by the policy.
  - name: states
    type: text_long
    label: States Configuration
    default: "[]"
    description: JSON array naming the slots to run, in order. Empty means probe state_1 upward.
  - name: forward_input_to_states
    type: boolean
    label: Forward Input To States
    default: false
    description: Give every slot the executor's original input as well as prior slot output.
  - name: flat_accumulation
    type: boolean
    label: Flat Accumulation
    default: false
    description: Merge slot outputs into one dict instead of namespacing them by slot.
comp_3.name: SEQUENTIAL EXECUTOR - FSM (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
comp_3.short_description: The engine of the Sequential Executor template. It holds the ordered steps and drives them

orchestration.description:
What it does Runs a series of steps one after another, in the order you wire them, passing each result to the next. It is the building block for a linear pipeline.

How it works Drop it into a flow as a single node and wire a component into each state slot. It runs slot one, hands the result to slot two, and so on. It can optionally loop the whole sequence until a condition you define is met or an iteration ceiling is reached, which turns a straight pipeline into a retry or refinement loop. The decision to continue, loop or stop is made by its policy component on every pass.

Configure (on the FSM component inside)
- States - the ordered slots, and what runs in each.
- Enable looping - repeat the sequence rather than running it once.
- Max iterations - the ceiling that stops a loop running away.
- Exit conditions - the tests that end the loop early when met.
- Forward input to states - give every step the original input as well as the previous
step's result.
- Flat accumulation - collect results into one flat object instead of nesting them per step.

In and out In: whatever the caller sent. Out: the result of the final step, or the accumulated results.

Use it when
- Work has to happen in a fixed order because each step needs the one before it.
- You want to retry or refine a result until it is good enough.
- A long process reads better as named steps than as one large component.
orchestration.name: SEQUENTIAL EXECUTOR (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
